cases.prompt: skillify this. This session I cleared the review feedback on a PR. I listed unresolved review threads, fixed 4 comments, replied to each thread with the commit that fixed it, resolved the threads, then re-checked the required checks until they were green. About 14 tool calls, and I had to handle one reviewer comment that was a question and not a change request.
cases.expected_output: Audits the session, and the gate passes: enough tool calls, a decision point, a gotcha, and a trigger phrase. Checks overlap with installed skills before writing. If an existing skill such as pr-review covers the workflow, proposes patching it and asks for confirmation instead of creating a duplicate. Writes nothing until the destination resolves.

cases.prompt: save this as a skill: I ran git log --oneline -5 to see the last five commits.
cases.expected_output: The gate rejects the work as a one-off or trivial wrapper. A single tool call with arguments is a tool, not a skill. Says the work did not warrant a skill and stops. Writes no file.

cases.prompt: make this proper. We just finished a 9-step, repeatable procedure for rotating an API key across three services, with a rollback branch when the second service rejects the new key. I am in a scratch directory with no skills folder, and I have not told you where skills go.
cases.expected_output: The gate passes, but the destination does not resolve. Stops all writes and asks the user for a directory path. Does not guess a path, and does not draft the skill file before the destination resolves.
